title: Test Drive
build: Decibel and Eagle Soft Incorporated side A, Eagle Soft Incorporated side B
uncounted: the RAM under the I/O area holds data, and game.json does not say what it is (kit/skills/c64/c64-reference, "RAM the CPU cannot see")

records.c: Relocated entry $2E68 and body length $0144 for CI.
Executable entry returns immediately. The selector reads the relocated address words following this byte as data.
Tagged address records used through the CI base at $06-$07. The code selects one of five three-byte records at $30B5, then uses two six-byte-per-car groups for the bitmap lists at $3163 and $325F.
Bytes addressed by the final descriptor at $2EB4. The selector reads car-specific pairs using the pointer loaded at $31DA.

Five groups of selected asset suffixes. The selector's loop skips zero entries and exits on $FF. Each group contains the car-specific short attribute and bitmap lists referenced by the preceding address records.
Relocated entry $2FB0 and body length $0713 for TS.
Reset the input latch, install the temporary IRQ, locate the graphic and car descriptions, and initialize selection to car zero.
Derive the disk item suffix from the selection at $40 plus ASCII '1'. Invoke GP and DP to prepare the selected car and wait for selector input.
Check the confirmation latch at $46, otherwise use the joystick index at $E2 and the table at $36B1. Advance or decrement $40 and wrap within five entries.
Stop the selector music through $6400 and release the car-select assets. Read the selected car's records through the module base $06 before preparing the driving display.
Copy 32 pages between the bitmap buffers selected by $34 and $35. Invoke the graphics loader and look up the car-specific assets by the selected car's suffix.
Synchronize the $D418 writes with the counter at $30 and lower the volume from 12 to zero.
Enable I/O, acknowledge the VIC-II interrupt, select the next raster phase and update horizontal scroll. At phase zero, service bank changes, selector joystick input and music.
Find the active-low direction nibble in the table at $36BA and put its index in $E2. OR an active fire button into the confirmation latch at $46.
Work with the selected offset and the visible bitmap addresses computed from the row and column tables.
Resolve the resource with the module lookup, read dimensions and position from its six-byte header, apply the current animation offsets, then draw the bitmap at the selected bank.
Call UJ with the selected two-byte asset ID on the stack, then free the reusable graphic item identified by the self-modifying operands at $3647 and $3649.
Nine active-low direction patterns read by the input loop at $3470.
